reason: r64 changes the bar's length rule: the fill is measured inside the tier band the points sit in, so the bar refills at every colour change - MH World's per-tier gauge - while the game keeps colouring it. The band's ceiling is clipped to mMaxSharpness, which is the whole answer for Sharpness+1/+2, HonedBlade, Bolreaver/Hellblade souls and the level-12 cap: a raised maximum stops the top band partway through its tier, and there it reads full. The cut, the shade and the colour code are untouched; the fill feeds the same cut_box and dim_box. No settings panel. The band comes from binary search on the game's own points-to-tier function uPlayerBase::calculateSharpnessType (main+0x29cdfc), so no weapon, level or kireaji table layout is read by the mod and the game's own gates apply - the fixed-tier state answers tier 0 for any points, and the fill is then current/maximum, what the accepted build drew. That function dereferences player+0x13c4 (main+0x29ce34) and then +0x4d4 (main+0x27c848, main+0x27c84c) with no check, so its 32-byte window is a required signature and, before any native call, the fill re-derives the player from the session and requires it to equal the capture, requires read_gauge with a positive maximum, and requires both pointers to read. Any failure, and any native call refused, yields no ratio: clip off, native gauge untouched, shade width 0. 29 host fixtures pass, including the tester's logged point sequence at kireaji row 10 and the buffed maxima; verify PASSED with 33 signature windows; the accepted tree (6 nodes, 7-word map, 13 records) is unchanged. RUNTIME: ran on Eden 2026-11-02 with the packaged payload installed, and the player accepted the bar as played for testing steps 1, 2 and 5 ("from playing and look at the visuals it looks right, but my current gameplay only satisfy no 1,2, and 5"). Steps 3 (Sharpness+1/+2) and 4 (Heavy Polish) were not exercised, no photo was supplied, the build logs no fill line, and this run's log has one insertion and one teardown at a quest end, so the per-area re-insertion is not exercised by it. No distribution approval: it stays a DEVELOPMENT candidate.
runtime_test: Eden run of 2026-11-02 with the installed NRO matching the packaged payload (a5f6f2c9b263a608331597e88c8d7d39b9c62943f96fcf082e55af36019e82ae, Forge 1.5.1, 9 plugin NRO loads, the same count as the accepted r63 session). Three MSG r64 lines: gauge row check stopped at stage 21 at 13.035483 (the hub, before any gauge HUD); scissor mask inserted at 155.176840 with entries=7 and records=13 and dim= and clip= non-zero, so the shade went in; inserted mask's links lost (1 times) at 1101.645590, with the game's save-data commits at 1111.848609 to 1111.935845 placing that teardown at a quest end, and no insertion after it. No guest exception, no insertion failure, no 'shade blade not added'. Against the r63 session the only new host-side line is HW.Memory <Error> Unmapped @ 0x00000082609400 (size = 48) at 1139.120422, inside the emulator's exit path after the RomFS patch burst at 1138.743248 and 4.34 s before ForceStop, with two Service.NVDRV pin-count warnings; the renderer Critical counts match the r63 session (maxwell_3d.cpp:392 45 vs 57, texture_cache.h:2196 10 vs 10, hle_ipc.cpp:339 1 vs 1, software_keyboard 1 vs 1), and r64's log has no host SIGSEGV after ForceStop. The player's report: "from playing and look at the visuals it looks right, but my current gameplay only satisfy no 1,2, and 5", so testing steps 1, 2 and 5 are satisfied and steps 3 (Sharpness+1/+2) and 4 (Heavy Polish) were not exercised. The build logs no fill line, so the log carries no band number: the acceptance is the player's eye. The accepted drawing of the cut and the shade remains accepted r62's Eden run of 2026-11-01 at the red tier (crop sha256 bb02addc7e2fe678977f453a08af0fcffdf7d6d68fc8e708dfc62329d16a1fdb). Log copy work/modern-sharpness-gauge/runs/r64-eden-2026-11-02.txt sha256 dff4e64cd8191651f67e44762263c0f825c9c153e993d3e6b481d88efc7369b8, extract sha256 b5b2e2e2b051a1d15463d4fc9684832a808500a2d47ad5f71ff8e59cbfbaf67d. limitations: the fill is accepted by the player's eye on the bar, not by a recorded number: the build logs no fill line, so no run carries a band value
the raised-maximum band ends have no runtime check: the r64 run did not exercise Sharpness+1/+2, and no saved log was identified as using a Sharpness skill
Heavy Polish over the banded bar has no runtime check
the per-area re-insertion is unproven for r64: its log has one insertion and one teardown at a quest end
the fill calls native code about twice per frame per band search on the draw thread; that thread is one thread by static reading and unconfirmed at runtime

mSharpnessType changes inside adjustSharpness and the bar reads it live, but the sequence driver's order against the draw is unread, so a tier drop could show one frame of a full bar in the old colour
the fixed-tier state (player+0x13cc low nibble >> 3) answers tier 0 for any points and its meaning is unread; the band design handles it without knowing it
the clip mask's bit 17 is the transform gate in main+0xa4964c / main+0xa4969c; what the shade looks like once the clip is composed rests on accepted r62's red-tier crop
bar_sampler= and dim_sampler= are reads of the low nibble of +0x108: equal numbers prove the copy was given the bar's style byte, not that the two halves filter identically on screen
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and the old 4-word block still leaks
the coloured part keeps the glow's halo (Txt_sharpefx at PosX 6, PosY -6, 88x32, alpha 120) and the dark part has none: the Phase 5 design question, asked and left open
the worn blade at the orange tier: the accepted crop is the red tier and no retained Eden log window keeps an orange band line, so orange rides the same setter path unseen
the bar rect other than 110..238: the scaled cut offsets have only been seen where they reproduce the measured numbers
never exercised: the root destructor hook has fired in no saved log; ARM fixtures for insertion and allocation failure are not written

evidence.static_summary: r64: pinned toolchain build; 29 host fixtures passed; verify.py PASSED with 33 NSO signature windows, a unique hook window, the exact export set, resolved imports only, no MSR in the disassembly, no DT_TEXTREL and a one-file payload. The fill is now (current - floor) * 10000 / (ceiling - floor) inside the tier band, with ceiling clipped to mMaxSharpness; the band is found by binary search on uPlayerBase::calculateSharpnessType (main+0x29cdfc), a signature-gated call behind three safety gates (the session's own player equal to the capture, a positive maximum, and both pointers that function dereferences read through the mapping check). Fixtures reproduce the tester's logged samples (150 10000, 131 500, 130 10000, 100 2500, 90 10000, 8 888, 0 0 at maximum 150 on kireaji row 10), the full top band at maxima 400/425/450, the zero-width `450, 450` band, constant-tier-0 equal to current/maximum, an unreadable probe yielding no ratio, and every probe inside 0..=maximum. The accepted tree is untouched: 6 nodes, 7-word object array, (6 << 4) | 8 = 104 bytes = 13 records. The native facts behind it are re-verified against the original bytes by work/modern-sharpness-gauge/scripts/verify_tier_gauge.py. See EVIDENCE.json, DEVELOPMENT.md and work/modern-sharpness-gauge/TIER_GAUGE_RESEARCH.md.
